content.title: Time for the module challenge! 🎯
content.body:
You've made it through all three lessons — now let's see what stuck.

This quiz covers everything from the module:
• What programming is and why it matters
• How computers follow instructions (and why bugs happen)
• What Python is and where it's used

Take your time — there's no timer. Every question has an explanation after you answer, so you'll learn from any mistakes as you go.

quiz.question: A program is a list of instructions that a computer follows in order.

options.text: True
False

quiz.explanation: Exactly right. A program is a precise, ordered list of instructions — the computer carries them out step by step, from top to bottom.

quiz.question: Which of these best describes what "processing" means in the Input → Processing → Output model?

options.text: Taking information into the program
Showing a result on screen
The computer doing something with the input
Writing the code

quiz.explanation: Processing is the middle step — the computer takes what came in and does something with it (calculates, decides, transforms) before producing an output.

quiz.question: Your robot instructions say "1. Pour the juice. 2. Open the bottle." What happens?

options.text: The robot opens the bottle first, because it's smart
The robot pours the juice successfully
The robot asks you what to do
The robot tries to pour from a closed bottle

quiz.explanation: Computers follow instructions in the exact order you write them. Step 1 is "pour the juice" — so it tries, even though the bottle is still closed.

quiz.question: What is a bug in a program?

options.text: A program that is too long
A mistake in the code that makes it behave unexpectedly
A feature that is too hard to use
A computer that is broken

quiz.explanation: A bug is a mistake in your code — a missing step, wrong order, or typo — that makes the program do something you didn't intend. All programmers write bugs. The skill is fixing them.

quiz.question: What is an algorithm?

options.text: A type of computer chip
A kind of bug
A precise, step-by-step plan for solving a problem
A programming language

quiz.explanation: An algorithm is your plan before you write code — a clear, step-by-step recipe for solving a problem. It's how every programmer thinks before typing anything.

quiz.question: Python was named after the snake.

options.text: True
False

quiz.explanation: False! Python was named after Monty Python, a British comedy group. The snake connection is just a fun coincidence.

quiz.question: Which of these is Python actually used for in the real world?

options.text: Designing physical computer chips
Only learning to code — it's not used professionally
AI tools, data analysis, and powering platforms like YouTube
Writing the firmware inside a fridge

quiz.explanation: Python is used by NASA, YouTube, Instagram, AI researchers, and game developers. It's a professional-grade language that's also approachable for beginners.

quiz.question: You want to build a quiz game but it feels too big. What's the programmer's approach?

options.text: Write all the code at once and hope for the best
Give up — it's too complicated
Find someone else to build it
Break it into small pieces: one question, check the answer, keep score, repeat

quiz.explanation: Breaking a big problem into small, manageable pieces is one of the most important skills in programming. Every expert does this — it's not just for beginners.
